analytic_steps: Exact negative overlap numerator equals -1+(4/5)d^beta-r y+epsilon x, denominator 1+d^beta+y+x.
On [0,1], d^beta=1+O(epsilon), r=-1/3+O(epsilon), and denominator >=1, giving uniform O(epsilon) error.
Differentiated high-state term contributes O(L epsilon); other errors remain O(epsilon), validating the separate derivative bound.
Full-premise sign theorem fixes b<0 below bath; amplitude derivative is -b derivative there.
Initial amplitude derivative is positive of order L; bath overlap derivative positive gives negative amplitude derivative approaching bath.

At most two stationary zeros counting multiplicity with opposite derivative endpoint signs implies exactly one simple interior maximum; a tangency in addition would require multiplicity at least three.
For each fixed positive beta the limiting leading ratio decreases strictly; uniform convergence excludes a maximizing beta bounded away from zero.
If L beta at the maximum remained bounded, x would stay bounded below and the positive order-L normalization derivative could not cancel; hence L beta tends infinity.
Exact leading derivative numerator after positive multiplier 15(2+y+x)^2 is x[(10L-5a)y-6L]-13ay.
At beta_m tending zero the x coefficient behaves like4L; derivative remainder O(L epsilon) produces an O(epsilon) absolute x correction.
Solve for x=13a/(4L)[1+O(beta_m+1/L)]; L epsilon is smaller than these algebraic scales.
Logarithm yields 2L beta_m=log(4L/(13a))+O(beta_m+1/L). Absorb beta_m to establish O(logL/L) before sharpening the remainder.
Taylor expansion of leading amplitude relative to2/45 has coefficients -13a/6 for beta and -1/3 for x, with quadratic mixed remainder.
Infinite-hot amplitude equals1/30+O(epsilon); reciprocal expansion gives gain coefficient13a/(16L) times[log(4L/(13a))+1].
Remainder O(logL^2/L^2) includes beta error, x relative error, and second-order Taylor terms; exponentially small epsilon is dominated.
Finite-hot plot beta_h=L^-2 has x_h=e^-2/L, so numerator differs from infinite-hot by O(1/L); leading supremum same, subleading curves differ.
Independent100-digit numerical differentiation and bisection reproduce five CSV maxima and their energy spans; residual table is diagnostic only.
scope: Unnumbered large-energy expansion and quarter-plot maxima; other figures remain separately pending.
